fields.h1: Build Finance Automation Around the Numbers You Watch
fields.hero_description: Build finance automation that watches cash and the close, and sends each exception to the person who owns it.
fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds for a Finance Team
fields.features_subheading: Each check runs against the systems your team already keeps, and every miss reaches a named owner before month end.
fields.feature_1:
Rules written the way you would say them

Describe a check in a sentence, such as a balance floor or an approval limit. Emergent builds the app, its database and its logic from that prompt, and a new prompt changes a rule.
fields.feature_2:
Your ledger and bank data, connected

The app connects to QuickBooks, Xero, NetSuite, Stripe, and any other tool with an API, and syncs data both ways. Balances and entries come straight from the records your team keeps.
fields.feature_3:
AI that reads invoices and statements

An AI step reads uploaded invoices and bank statements into fields such as the amount and the payee. A field the AI is unsure of goes to a person on your team before a check uses it.
fields.feature_4:
Reminders that move up when unanswered

Each exception reaches its owner in Slack or by email. You set the day a reminder goes out and how long an item can sit unanswered before it moves to the owner's manager.
fields.feature_5:
One live board for open exceptions

The dashboard updates as balances and requests change, with every record saved in a database you own. Month-end review starts from rows the app already stored, not a spreadsheet.
fields.feature_6:
The finance app's code, in your GitHub

Export the full code of the app to your GitHub repository on paid plans. A developer can read each rule and review every change to it, the same way they review other code.
fields.why_title: Why Build Finance Automation With Emergent?
fields.why_description: Emergent builds each finance check and the app around it from a prompt, on a database you own, with no task cap when runs pile up at month end.

plan.angle: The top 10 are vendor guides and suites that define finance automation in general terms. This page shows four finance-team automations beyond the ledger work that sibling pages own, drawn as working screens at one company, Quarrybrook Cycle Co.: a 7:00 AM cash check across 3 bank accounts that flags the operating account under its $250,000 floor, an intercompany check that holds the October close over a $4,500 gap, one intake form for finance requests where any credit memo over $1,000 goes to the controller, and forecast updates from 9 department heads with reminders to the 2 still missing. The FAQ answers the example, setup, close, entity and cost questions builders compare.
tab_stories: At 7:00 AM the app reads balances from Quarrybrook's 3 bank accounts, totals $1,284,600, and because the operating account sits at $186,400, under its $250,000 floor, it sends controller Elliot Pellegarde a direct message with the balance.

Before the October close, the app compares the balances the two Quarrybrook companies hold with each other: Manufacturing shows $96,300 due from Retail, Retail shows $91,800 owed, and the $4,500 gap holds both closes until accountants Brunhild Rasku and Tomas Fontanez explain it.

Teams outside finance send refunds, cost center requests and credit memos through one form; 23 came in this week, and a $2,400 credit memo from sales rep Corin Drummellier goes to the controller because any credit memo over $1,000 needs him.

By business day 5 each month, 9 department heads update their next-quarter forecast in a form; 7 are in, the app reminds the heads of Marketing and Facilities, and FP&A lead Benedek Szalo sees the 2 departments marked missing on the dashboard.
